title: Using Claude AI for Chip Design - Semiwiki
gist: After dozens of conversations at the Design Automation Conference in Long Beach, Daniel Nenni reports Claude was the common denominator in every discussion of AI in the chip-design flow, and lays out where it works as an engineering copilot — spec decomposition, RTL drafting, and especially verification — while insisting correctness still comes from trusted EDA engines and human review.

themes.theme: Claude as the default AI entry point in silicon

insights.claim: In dozens of conversations with semiconductor professionals at the Design Automation Conference in Long Beach about AI in the chip-design workflow, Claude emerged as the common denominator in every conversation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Model standardization inside a high-value vertical is a durable revenue signal for Anthropic and shapes which EDA integrations get built first.
insights.quote: Claude emerged as the common denominator in every conversation.
insights.locator: After speaking with dozens of semiconductor professionals

insights.claim: AI use in the chip design flow is still at the tip of the iceberg, so the practical recommendation for teams under management pressure to adopt AI is to start with Claude as an easy entry point.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Adoption is top-down mandated and early — implies the AI-EDA spend curve is ahead of measurable productivity, not behind it.
insights.quote: We’re still at the tip of the iceberg when it comes to using AI in the design flow.
insights.locator: After speaking with dozens of semiconductor professionals

insights.claim: Claude should be treated as an engineering copilot across specification analysis, RTL development, verification, automation and debug — not as an autonomous replacement for EDA tools or experienced engineers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames the realistic TAM: AI augments EDA seats rather than displacing tool licenses, so incumbent EDA revenue is not directly at risk near term.
insights.quote: It should not be treated as an autonomous replacement for EDA tools or experienced engineers.
insights.locator: Today, Claude can support semiconductor design

insights.claim: The value of an LLM in chip design comes from translating design intent into structured artifacts, reasoning across large codebases, and orchestrating repeatable tool-driven workflows.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A three-part test for evaluating any AI-EDA startup's claims: artifact generation, codebase-scale reasoning, and tool orchestration.
insights.quote: Its value comes from translating design intent into structured artifacts, reasoning across large codebases, and orchestrating repeatable tool-driven workflows.
insights.locator: Today, Claude can support semiconductor design

themes.theme: Spec decomposition catches ambiguity before code

insights.claim: Feeding a module specification, interface protocol, timing assumptions, reset behavior and corner cases to Claude yields a requirements table, microarchitecture proposal, register map, state-machine description and implementation checklist, exposing ambiguity before coding begins.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shifting bug discovery left of RTL is where the cost savings actually live — the metric to demand from AI-EDA vendors is bugs found pre-code.
insights.quote: This step exposes ambiguity before coding begins.
insights.locator: A productive starting point is specification decomposition

insights.claim: Concrete ambiguity classes an LLM catches in specs include undefined behavior during simultaneous read and write, inconsistent clock-domain assumptions, and missing rules for backpressure and error recovery.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: These are exactly the defects that historically escape to silicon; a tool that reliably flags them has quantifiable respin-avoidance value.
insights.locator: For example, Claude can identify undefined behavior

themes.theme: RTL generation: bounded tasks and mandatory review

insights.claim: Claude is suited to drafting synthesizable SystemVerilog or VHDL for bounded blocks — finite-state machines, arbiters, FIFOs, protocol adapters, CSR blocks and parameterized datapaths — and is most effective making small reviewable changes rather than whole subsystems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Bounded-block generation limits realistic productivity gains; claims of full-subsystem autogeneration should be treated as unproven.
insights.quote: Claude is most effective when asked to make small, reviewable changes rather than generate an entire complex subsystem at once.
insights.locator: Claude can then draft synthesizable SystemVerilog

insights.claim: Generated RTL must be reviewed for width errors, unintended latches, incomplete assignments, signedness problems, unsafe clock-domain crossings and reset inconsistencies — a fixed review burden that does not disappear with better prompting.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Human review overhead caps net headcount savings from AI-generated RTL; model the productivity gain as partial, not multiplicative.
insights.locator: The generated RTL must be reviewed

insights.claim: Verification is described as often the strongest application of Claude in chip design, spanning test plans, SystemVerilog Assertions, constrained-random sequences, scoreboards, functional coverage models and UVM component skeletons.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Verification is the biggest labor pool in design — concentrate AI-EDA investment exposure there rather than in synthesis or place-and-route.
insights.quote: Verification is often the strongest application.
insights.locator: Verification is often the strongest application

insights.claim: Language-model assistance is most useful when connected to authoritative verification engines — simulation, formal analysis, regression management, debug — rather than used standalone, which is why commercial EDA platforms are combining generative and agentic AI with those engines.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Incumbents that own the golden engines hold the strategic position; pure-LLM verification startups must attach to them or be commoditized.
insights.quote: language-model assistance is most useful when connected to authoritative verification engines rather than used alone

insights.claim: Claude Code can run an agentic loop inside a chip repository — modify RTL, run lint, interpret diagnostics, launch focused tests and produce a patch with rationale — when lint, elaboration, simulation, formal, synthesis and STA commands are wrapped in controlled scripts.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The unlock is script-wrapped tool access, not model capability — companies with clean automated flows will capture AI gains first.
insights.locator: Claude Code can operate inside a repository

insights.claim: Model Context Protocol connections or custom tool interfaces can expose internal documentation, issue trackers, regression dashboards and approved EDA commands to the model while preserving access controls.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: MCP is becoming the integration standard in a conservative, IP-sensitive industry — a moat consideration for whichever model vendor owns it.

themes.theme: Physical design limits and governance gates

insights.claim: For physical design, Claude can summarize synthesis and place-and-route reports and hypothesize causes such as excessive fanout or overaggressive clock targets, but optimization decisions must be validated in the actual flow because PPA depends on libraries, process corners, extraction and tool settings a model cannot reliably infer.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Backend physical design stays defensible against LLM disruption — the sign-off data dependency is a structural barrier protecting incumbent tool value.
insights.quote: the optimization decision must be validated through the actual flow

insights.claim: A disciplined workflow requires storing project rules in a repository instruction file and requiring Claude to cite the specification paragraph behind every behavioral change, with version control, mandatory human review, lint, CDC/RDC, formal, timing, equivalence and physical verification as gates.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Citation-to-spec plus deterministic sign-off gates is the emerging governance template; vendors without it will stall in enterprise procurement.
insights.quote: Never accept plausible-looking RTL merely because it compiles.

insights.claim: IP and security constraints — model deployment policy, data retention, source-code exposure, foundry information, third-party IP and export-controlled material — are a first-order adoption gate, handled with enterprise gateways, restricted repositories, permission-limited tool calls and audit trails.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Export-control and foundry-data sensitivity favor on-prem or gateway-mediated deployments — a structural advantage for vendors offering private deployment.

insights.claim: The bottom line is that Claude works as a reasoning and automation layer around established chip-design methods, while correctness still comes from executable specifications, trusted EDA tools, measured results and accountable engineering review.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The value split favors tool vendors owning the golden reference and model vendors owning the orchestration layer — neither displaces the other soon.
insights.quote: Claude works best as a reasoning and automation layer around established chip-design methods.
